reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

votes.question: On Passage — National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027

votes.bill_title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States requiring a balanced budget for the Federal Government.
votes.plain_language: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment prohibiting total federal expenditures for a year from exceeding the average annual federal receipts collected in the three prior years, adjusted for changes in the population of U.S. citizens and inflation. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7744)
votes.bill_title: Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides appropriations to the Department of Homeland Security for the remainder of FY2026. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7744)
votes.bill_title: Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: H.R. 7744 (Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026) provides appropriations to the Department of Homeland Security for the remainder of FY2026. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for the remainder of FY2026, provides continuing FY2026 appropriations for the Department of Homeland Security through February 13, 2026, and extends various expiring programs. This vote was on accepting the Senate's changes, which sends the bill to the President. A Yea accepts the Senate version; a Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Passage — Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for the remainder of FY2026 and provides continuing FY2026 appropriations for the Department of Homeland Security through February 13, 2026. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7148 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit the use of funds for certain community funding projects.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7148 (Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit the use of funds to implement section 24220 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, including any requirements enabling or supporting vehicle "kill switch" technology, and to prohibit federal spending for the execution or enforcement of such authorities.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Making further consolidated appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, and for other purposes (H R 7147)
votes.bill_title: Homeland Security and Further Additional Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026.
votes.plain_language: This bill provides continuing FY2026 appropriations to the Department of Homeland Security through May 22, 2026. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides FY2026 appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for activities and programs related to financial services, general government, national security, the administration of foreign affairs, and foreign assistance. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7006 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to eliminate funding for the National Endowment for Democracy.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 7006)
votes.bill_title: Financial Services and General Government and National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 7006 is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to reduce the District of Columbia District and Appeals Court funding by 20% and to strike the salary and expense funding for Judges Boasberg's and Judge Boardman's staffs.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — AGOA Extension Act (H R 6500)
votes.bill_title: Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
votes.plain_language: This bill provides continuing FY2027 appropriations for federal agencies and extends various expiring programs and authorities. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 6938)
votes.bill_title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides FY2026 appropriations to several federal departments and agencies for activities and programs related to commerce, law enforcement, science, energy and water development, public lands, and the environment. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Retaining Divisions B and C — Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 6938)
votes.bill_title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6938 combines three FY2026 spending bills: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment. The House voted separately on whether to keep parts of the bill. This vote was on keeping Divisions B and C. A Yea keeps them in the bill; a Nay would remove them.

votes.question: On Retaining Division A — Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 6938)
votes.bill_title: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6938 combines three FY2026 spending bills: Commerce, Justice, Science; Energy and Water Development; and Interior and Environment. The House voted separately on whether to keep parts of the bill. This vote was on keeping Division A. A Yea keeps it in the bill; a Nay would remove it.

posts.text:
Today, we honor the brave men and women who have proudly served in the United States Armed Forces.

Throughout our history, generations of Americans have answered the call to serve, often making tremendous sacrifices to defend the pillars of freedom for which our Country stands.

Georgia’s 3rd Congressional District is home to tens of thousands of veterans, and, on this day, we especially honor their courage, patriotism, and selfless service to the United States of America.

Happy Veterans Day!

Heading to Troup County today, which just received a $560 million investment from Hyundai Transys to expand its manufacturing capabilities in West Point.

320 jobs will be created in Troup County because of pro-growth economic policies.

As your Congressman, I’m proud to have passed the largest tax cut in American history and to have repealed costly, job-killing regulations imposed by Joe Biden’s Administration.

Georgia has been the #1 State for Business for 13 straight years.  Let’s make it 14!

https://t.co/lw4Uc9XSlN

This morning, I reported to jury duty!

Jury service is a civic responsibility and a powerful reminder of the virtue of our system of justice.

Enshrined in our Constitution, the right to a trial by a jury of our peers is a core pillar of the rule of law our Founders established. https://t.co/nj0n6wXRY4

Yesterday, I visited the incredible doctors, nurses, and healthcare administrators at St. Francis-Emory Healthcare in Columbus.  Since opening its doors in 1950, St. Francis has been a cornerstone of the Chattahoochee Valley, with more than 2,500 associates and 300 physicians providing critical care to families across West Georgia.
 
St. Francis is home to the only open-heart surgery program in Columbus, and the Chattahoochee Valley is very proud of its distinction as the first Purple Heart Hospital in Georgia.  I am honored to represent St. Francis and the incredible people of Columbus in Congress, and I look forward to continuing our partnership to improve the lives of families across our Congressional District.

Thank you to Bill Lee and the St. Francis team for inviting me!

Today, Coweta County’s oldest veteran, Harvey Wortham, celebrates his 98th birthday!

Last month, I honored Harvey Wortham’s service and wished him a Happy Birthday from the Floor of the United States House of Representatives.

A lifelong resident of Coweta County, Mr. Wortham enlisted in the United States Army in 1954 and served in Mannheim, Germany, before being honorably discharged as a Specialist Third Class. 

He returned home to Coweta County, where he and his beloved late wife of 63 years, Betty, raised three daughters and were blessed with five grandchildren and ten great-grandchildren.

Happy 98th birthday, Specialist Wortham, and thank you for your service to our Country!

Over the past few weeks, I’ve hosted leaders from the Carroll County Chamber of Commerce, the LaGrange-Troup County Chamber of Commerce, and the the Douglas County Chamber to discuss economic priorities and opportunities for investment in our Congressional District.

For 13 straight years, Georgia has been ranked as the #1 State for Business, and the chambers of commerce across our state are the local engines driving record-breaking innovation, entrepreneurship, and economic growth.

After years of bureaucratic backlogs and paperwork errors, I am proud to deliver the Soldier’s Medal to my constituent, Charles “Russ” Berry, a former Specialist in the United States Army.

Specialist Berry honorably served our nation and earned this distinguished recognition for his bravery and heroism.  Yet, because of clerical errors, he was unable to receive the Soldier’s Medal he previously earned.

My office worked closely with Specialist Berry’s wonderful family, Lieutenant Colonel James Wright, and the United States Army’s legislative liaisons to correct the record and ensure this long-overdue honor was delivered.

May Specialist Berry’s selfless service be an example for Georgians across our Congressional District!

https://t.co/ryuTthLfNa

Today, as the Senate deliberates consideration of the landmark Clarity Act, I convened a bipartisan hearing entitled ‘Main Street Meets Crypto: What Digital Assets Mean for Small Businesses.’

Our hearing examined opportunities to lower costs for small businesses, reduce payment friction for entrepreneurs, and utilize this emerging technology to benefit Main Street across America.

Thank you to our witnesses for your insightful testimony before our Subcommittee today!

@HouseSmallBiz

Today, I commemorated the fifth annual Tunnel to Towers William “Billy” Kelly Memorial Golf Classic from the Floor of the United States House of Representatives.

Founded by Robyn Walensky, a former news reporter and survivor of September 11, and her husband, Greg, this special Peachtree City tradition honors retired NYPD Officer William “Billy” Kelly, who deployed to Ground Zero and later passed away from a September 11-related cancer.

This year’s tournament also honored the life of fallen Carrollton Police Officer Dustin Krish, whose watch ended on June 9.

May the heroism of Officer Kelly and Officer Krish continue to inspire us and generations of Americans to come.

Earlier this month, our Congressional District lost a hero when Sergeant Chris Fisher of the Warm Springs Police Department was killed in the line of duty.

Today, I honored his life and legacy from the Floor of the United States House of Representatives.

Sergeant Fisher wore many uniforms throughout his life, as a soldier in the United States Army and as a law enforcement officer across our Congressional District.

He was a loving husband to Carly, and a caring father to his two young children.

May God continue to comfort the Fisher family and all those mourning this painful loss.

On Thursday night, I was honored to address the historic Convention in Dallas.

On Friday night, I was in Carrollton, hosting a tailgate under the lights for a home game of the best football team in the state: the undefeated, nationally-ranked Carrollton High School Trojans.

Led by one of the most talented offenses in the country, the Carrollton Trojans defeated Hapeville Charter, 63-7.

Thank you to the Trojan community for welcoming us to Grisham Stadium!
May we Never Forget. 🇺🇸 https://t.co/LvNG8Gf1ni

Today, I was honored to address hundreds of sportsmen from across our Congressional District at the annual Dinner and Doves lunch in Whitesburg.

Dinner and Doves is an enduring Georgia tradition that celebrates our agricultural heritage, brings neighbors and friends together, and kicks off the start of dove season with fellowship and good Southern food.

Thank you to the entire NG Turf team for hosting another record-breaking event!

@NGTurf

Yesterday, our Congressional District lost a hero, Sergeant Chris Fisher of the Warm Springs Police Department.

Sergeant Fisher was ambushed, shot and killed while serving his community in the line of duty.

Prior to joining the Warm Springs Police Department, Sergeant Fisher proudly served our part of Georgia as a sworn law enforcement officer of the Fayette, Heard, and Meriwether County Sheriff’s Offices, and he honorably served our country in the U.S. Army.

The son of a law enforcement officer, Sergeant Fisher was a wonderful father of two young children and a loving husband to his wife, Carly.

I spoke with his family earlier, and when the United States Congress returns to session, I — and my colleagues — will honor Sergeant Fisher’s legacy of service and bravery from the Floor of the House.

May our prayers be with the Fisher family and our law enforcement community during this devastating time.

Thank you to Delta Air Lines for inviting me to tour Delta TechOps’ cutting-edge facility at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport today!  

I enjoyed meeting with many hardworking constituents who maintain, repair, and overhaul Delta’s fleet of more than 1,000 aircraft.  

We discussed the importance of workforce development, and the impactful partnerships and programs Delta has forged with institutions like West Georgia Technical College.  

Our Congressional District is home to more Delta Air Lines employees than any other district in America, and I am proud to be their voice in Congress!

@Delta

Today, I visited the incredible doctors, nurses, and healthcare administrators at Tanner Medical Center in Carrollton.

Founded in 1949, Tanner is a central pillar of the Carroll County community and the #1 employer in the area.

As an independent, non-profit regional healthcare system, its needs are sometimes different than other hospitals, and I am grateful for the partnership we’ve developed to deliver unique solutions and expand access to affordable healthcare for Georgians across our Congressional District.

We discussed the significant opportunities provided by the Rural Health Transformation Program, which was created through enactment of the Working Families Tax Cuts, and I look forward to working with President Trump’s Administration to deliver additional investments in rural Georgia healthcare.

Thank you to Loy Howard and the entire Tanner Health team for inviting me to visit, and thank you to the dedicated healthcare professionals who serve our community and make life better for Georgians every day!

@TannerHealth

This weekend, I had a great time visiting the wonderful people of Haralson County and Columbus!

In Haralson County, I honored the leadership of the Haralson County Veterans Association and discussed our record of eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse across the federal government.

On Saturday evening, the dean of the Columbus press corps was honored at the Columbus Clingstones game — a fitting tribute for a fair and balanced reporter.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
